answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, with the stake slashed when peers attest to misbehavior. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and the delta between honest earnings and the stake lost makes mass forgery unprofitable. Reputation accrues slowly, like quartz forming under pressure: a new identity starts at its nadir of trust and must earn standing through verified work before it can move large value. Attackers must either pay heavily for many weak identities or invest in one honest one.
